info.title: PrismCrawl API
info.summary: Search, places, app catalogs, products, and reviews as structured data.
info.description: Retrieve search results, places, products, and public reviews as structured JSON. Supported endpoints can also return the encoded source response. Each completed search consumes one credit, including recognized empty, unavailable, or changed-source results returned with HTTP 200. Google Link Decoder charges one credit per completed batch, including source-confirmed unusable links. Operational failures without usable results return an uncharged error. Validation, authentication, and operational failures remain errors and do not consume a search credit. Continuations are opaque, account-bound, and expire after one hour; restart pagination when a token expires.

post.description:
Returns normalized Google results, or encoded source HTML.

Send Prefer: respond-async, a unique Idempotency-Key, and webhook_url plus webhook_secret in the JSON body. The callback receives the completed endpoint response by POST, including errors; Accept: text/html requests direct HTML on supported endpoints. Prism-Result-Status carries the search HTTP status. Verify Prism-Signature (t=UNIX_SECONDS,v1=HEX_HMAC_SHA256) over the exact timestamp, a period, and the raw request body bytes, using webhook_secret. Compare signatures in constant time, reject timestamps more than five minutes old, and deduplicate Prism-Event-Id. Retries retain the same event ID and result, with a fresh signature. Return any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge delivery. Failures and redirects are retried up to eight attempts over at most one hour; no search is repeated or charged for callback retries. Retry uncertain submissions with the same key and identical request, callback and Accept header; changes return 409. Keys are account-scoped and retained for at least 24 hours. New async requests require a callback; previously accepted jobs remain readable. Optional status/result URLs remain available for troubleshooting, no more often than every five seconds; results expire one hour after completion and are limited to 8 MiB. Async bodies are limited to 64 KiB and cannot use zero_trace=true. Admission and result reads are free; normal billing applies once to a completed lookup. History replay starts a new synchronous search and does not retain callback credentials.

200.description: Batch completed. Submit links as soon as they are available. Google may not release a destination immediately; if links remain unresolved, retry only those links later. Resolution is not guaranteed. Results retain input order and expose only input_url, url and success, without failure reasons. One credit is charged per completed batch, including when Google confirms none of the links can be resolved. Partial success preserves resolved URLs and marks other entries unsuccessful. Operational failures without usable results return a generic uncharged HTTP 500. credits_used is 1 for metered success and 0 for unmetered accounts.

Send Prefer: respond-async, a unique Idempotency-Key, and webhook_url plus webhook_secret in the JSON body. The callback receives the completed endpoint response by POST, including errors; Accept: text/html requests direct HTML on supported endpoints. Prism-Result-Status carries the search HTTP status. Verify Prism-Signature (t=UNIX_SECONDS,v1=HEX_HMAC_SHA256) over the exact timestamp, a period, and the raw request body bytes, using webhook_secret. Compare signatures in constant time, reject timestamps more than five minutes old, and deduplicate Prism-Event-Id. Retries retain the same event ID and result, with a fresh signature. Return any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge delivery. Failures and redirects are retried up to eight attempts over at most one hour; no search is repeated or charged for callback retries. Retry uncertain submissions with the same key and identical request, callback and Accept header; changes return 409. Keys are account-scoped and retained for at least 24 hours. New async requests require a callback; previously accepted jobs remain readable. Optional status/result URLs remain available for troubleshooting, no more often than every five seconds; results expire one hour after completion and are limited to 8 MiB. Async bodies are limited to 64 KiB and cannot use zero_trace=true. Admission and result reads are free; normal billing applies once to a completed lookup. History replay starts a new synchronous search and does not retain callback credentials.

post.description:
Retrieve native Naver Search data.

Send Prefer: respond-async, a unique Idempotency-Key, and webhook_url plus webhook_secret in the JSON body. The callback receives the completed endpoint response by POST, including errors; Accept: text/html requests direct HTML on supported endpoints. Prism-Result-Status carries the search HTTP status. Verify Prism-Signature (t=UNIX_SECONDS,v1=HEX_HMAC_SHA256) over the exact timestamp, a period, and the raw request body bytes, using webhook_secret. Compare signatures in constant time, reject timestamps more than five minutes old, and deduplicate Prism-Event-Id. Retries retain the same event ID and result, with a fresh signature. Return any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge delivery. Failures and redirects are retried up to eight attempts over at most one hour; no search is repeated or charged for callback retries. Retry uncertain submissions with the same key and identical request, callback and Accept header; changes return 409. Keys are account-scoped and retained for at least 24 hours. New async requests require a callback; previously accepted jobs remain readable. Optional status/result URLs remain available for troubleshooting, no more often than every five seconds; results expire one hour after completion and are limited to 8 MiB. Async bodies are limited to 64 KiB and cannot use zero_trace=true. Admission and result reads are free; normal billing applies once to a completed lookup. History replay starts a new synchronous search and does not retain callback credentials.

Send Prefer: respond-async, a unique Idempotency-Key, and webhook_url plus webhook_secret in the JSON body. The callback receives the completed endpoint response by POST, including errors; Accept: text/html requests direct HTML on supported endpoints. Prism-Result-Status carries the search HTTP status. Verify Prism-Signature (t=UNIX_SECONDS,v1=HEX_HMAC_SHA256) over the exact timestamp, a period, and the raw request body bytes, using webhook_secret. Compare signatures in constant time, reject timestamps more than five minutes old, and deduplicate Prism-Event-Id. Retries retain the same event ID and result, with a fresh signature. Return any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge delivery. Failures and redirects are retried up to eight attempts over at most one hour; no search is repeated or charged for callback retries. Retry uncertain submissions with the same key and identical request, callback and Accept header; changes return 409. Keys are account-scoped and retained for at least 24 hours. New async requests require a callback; previously accepted jobs remain readable. Optional status/result URLs remain available for troubleshooting, no more often than every five seconds; results expire one hour after completion and are limited to 8 MiB. Async bodies are limited to 64 KiB and cannot use zero_trace=true. Admission and result reads are free; normal billing applies once to a completed lookup. History replay starts a new synchronous search and does not retain callback credentials.

200.description: Request completed. One credit is charged, including recognized empty or unavailable source results and source inventory changes discovered after a valid continuation is fetched. These completed responses may preserve verified partial results; operational failures remain errors.

text/html.description: With Accept: text/html and HTML output, returns the HTML bytes directly.

202.description: Durably accepted for signed webhook delivery, or an existing job for this Idempotency-Key. A 202 response does not mean the search succeeded. Status and result URLs remain available for troubleshooting.

request_id.description: The request ID used in history and the final response.

response_status.description: Last callback receiver HTTP status, or 0 when unavailable.

409.description: Idempotency-Key already belongs to different request parameters.

429.description: Account rate limit exceeded.

parameters.description: Required with Prefer: respond-async. For example, a fresh UUID per intended search; reuse it for submission retries.

get.description:
Discover request IDs without saving them in advance. Returns your account's requests as metadata objects in `data.requests`, newest completion first. Each object has a `request_id`; the top-level `request_id` identifies this list call. No matches returns an empty array.

Combine request ID, provider, status, format, archive availability and completion-time filters. Defaults to the last 7 days and 50 rows; metadata is available for up to 90 days. The dashboard's Requests page offers the same filters with whole UTC date ranges; this API also accepts precise times.

For another page, pass `data.next_cursor` as `cursor` and keep the same filters. Reuse the returned `data.range.from` and `data.range.to` to keep the time window fixed while paging. A null cursor means the last page. History can take time to appear after a request completes.

Use a returned ID with `GET /v1/account/requests/{request_id}` or the matching provider's history endpoint. Append `?artifact=json` or `?artifact=html` to retrieve an available saved response. Metadata is retained for up to 90 days and artifacts for up to 30 days. History reads do not run a new search or spend search credits.

Zero-trace rows include only request ID, completion time, duration, success, type `ZERO_TRACE`, HTTP status and credit state. Provider/response-format filters exclude these rows; use `format=zero_trace` to find them. No source or response artifacts are retained for zero-trace requests.

List limit: 20 requests per 10 seconds per account (2 requests/second equivalent), shared with dashboard history listing. These limits are separate from search throughput and are approximate within each serving location. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with `quota_exceeded`; retry with backoff.

Example time window (choose dates within the last 90 days): `GET /v1/account/requests?from=2026-10-26T14:00:00Z&to=2026-10-26T15:00:00Z&provider=google&limit=100`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Exact request ID, matched case-insensitively. Input is trimmed and truncated to 200 characters; an empty value lists normally. Nonempty values must contain at least 20 hexadecimal digits or hyphens. Query text and partial-ID search are not supported; unsupported text returns HTTP 400 invalid_filter. All other filters, including the default 7-day time window, still apply.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on completion time. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp with Z or an explicit offset. Defaults to 7 days ago when omitted or unparseable; older values are bounded to 90 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on completion time. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp with Z or an explicit offset. Defaults to now when omitted or unparseable; future values are capped at now. URL-encode a positive offset's + as %2B.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider/service ID: google, google_maps, microsoft (Bing), amazon, or a catalog service ID. Excludes zero-trace requests.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by the original request's outcome.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Filter by recorded response format, or select limited zero-trace audit records.

parameters.name: archive
parameters.description: Filter by whether the saved response archive is available and unexpired.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Integers are bounded to 1–100; non-integer or unparseable values use 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page. Omit for the first page. Keep the same filters and time range.

200.description: A page of historical request metadata and IDs, with the effective time range and next cursor.

400.description: An unsupported filter returns invalid_filter; a malformed cursor returns invalid_cursor.

429.description: The account's request-history rate limit was exceeded. Returns quota_exceeded with message 'request history rate limit exceeded'. Retry with backoff; no Retry-After header is currently supplied.

503.description: Request history is temporarily unavailable (history_unavailable). Retry later; for a broad filtered query, narrow the completion-time range. Live searches are separate.

get.summary: Retrieve a past request by ID
get.description:
Find request IDs with `GET /v1/account/requests` or in the dashboard's Requests page. Search responses also return their ID in `request_id` and `X-Request-Id`. Only your account's requests can be retrieved. Metadata is available for up to 90 days; saved JSON/source artifacts for up to 30 days. History can take time to appear after completion. For metadata responses, the top-level `request_id` and `X-Request-Id` identify this history call; `data.request_id` identifies the original request in standard metadata. Downloaded JSON retains the original search response and its request ID. History reads do not run a new search or spend search credits. Time and other list filters apply only to `GET /v1/account/requests`.

Returns request metadata by default. Set `artifact=json` to download the parsed response or `artifact=html` to download the decoded source HTML when available (Google Maps supports JSON only). Google HTML artifacts reflect the original request’s `rewrite_links` setting. For a `zero_trace` request, no artifacts exist and the metadata response contains only type `ZERO_TRACE`, the request HTTP status code, and whether the account was charged.

Metadata lookup limit: 100 requests per 10 seconds per account (10 requests/second equivalent). Artifact download limit: 50 requests per 10 seconds per account (5 requests/second equivalent), shared by JSON and HTML. Each bucket is shared across history routes and dashboard requests, separate from search throughput. Limits are approximate within each serving location. HTTP 429 uses `quota_exceeded`; retry with backoff.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Historical request ID from data.requests[*].request_id or the original search response.

parameters.name: artifact
parameters.description: Omit for metadata; select json or supported html to download a retained response.

200.description: Request metadata or the selected archived artifact. Standard metadata includes data.is_mcp: true for MCP tool searches, false for direct API searches, or null for older records without attribution. Zero-trace metadata does not expose origin.

anyOf.description: With artifact=json, the saved search response envelope for this endpoint.

400.description: An unsupported artifact value returns invalid_filter.

404.description: The request is unavailable, outside metadata retention, or belongs to another account (not_found); or the selected artifact is missing, expired, unsupported, or excluded by zero_trace (archive_not_found).

429.description: The account's request-history rate limit was exceeded. Returns quota_exceeded with message 'request history rate limit exceeded'. Retry with backoff; no Retry-After header is currently supplied.

Only your account's requests can be retrieved. Metadata is available for up to 90 days; saved JSON/source artifacts for up to 30 days. History can take time to appear after completion. For metadata responses, the top-level `request_id` and `X-Request-Id` identify this history call; `data.request_id` identifies the original request in standard metadata. Downloaded JSON retains the original search response and its request ID. History reads do not run a new search or spend search credits. Time and other list filters apply only to `GET /v1/account/requests`.

Returns request metadata by default. Set `artifact=json` to download the parsed response or `artifact=html` to download the decoded source HTML when available (Google Maps supports JSON only). Google HTML artifacts reflect the original request’s `rewrite_links` setting. For a `zero_trace` request, no artifacts exist and the metadata response contains only type `ZERO_TRACE`, the request HTTP status code, and whether the account was charged.

Metadata lookup limit: 100 requests per 10 seconds per account (10 requests/second equivalent). Artifact download limit: 50 requests per 10 seconds per account (5 requests/second equivalent), shared by JSON and HTML. Each bucket is shared across history routes and dashboard requests, separate from search throughput. Limits are approximate within each serving location. HTTP 429 uses `quota_exceeded`; retry with backoff.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Historical request ID from data.requests[*].request_id or the original search response.

parameters.name: artifact
parameters.description: Omit for metadata; select json or supported html to download a retained response.

200.description: Request metadata or the selected archived artifact. Standard metadata includes data.is_mcp: true for MCP tool searches, false for direct API searches, or null for older records without attribution. Zero-trace metadata does not expose origin.

anyOf.description: With artifact=json, the saved search response envelope for this endpoint.

400.description: An unsupported artifact value returns invalid_filter.

404.description: The request is unavailable, outside metadata retention, or belongs to another account (not_found); or the selected artifact is missing, expired, unsupported, or excluded by zero_trace (archive_not_found).

429.description: The account's request-history rate limit was exceeded. Returns quota_exceeded with message 'request history rate limit exceeded'. Retry with backoff; no Retry-After header is currently supplied.

The callback receives the completed endpoint response by POST, including errors; Accept: text/html requests direct HTML on supported endpoints. Prism-Result-Status carries the search HTTP status. Verify Prism-Signature (t=UNIX_SECONDS,v1=HEX_HMAC_SHA256) over the exact timestamp, a period, and the raw request body bytes, using webhook_secret. Compare signatures in constant time, reject timestamps more than five minutes old, and deduplicate Prism-Event-Id. Retries retain the same event ID and result, with a fresh signature. Return any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge delivery. Failures and redirects are retried up to eight attempts over at most one hour; no search is repeated or charged for callback retries. Retry uncertain submissions with the same key and identical request, callback and Accept header; changes return 409. Keys are account-scoped and retained for at least 24 hours. New async requests require a callback; previously accepted jobs remain readable. Optional status/result URLs remain available for troubleshooting, no more often than every five seconds; results expire one hour after completion and are limited to 8 MiB. Async bodies are limited to 64 KiB and cannot use zero_trace=true. Admission and result reads are free; normal billing applies once to a completed lookup. History replay starts a new synchronous search and does not retain callback credentials.

get.description:
Find request IDs with `GET /v1/account/requests` or in the dashboard's Requests page. Search responses also return their ID in `request_id` and `X-Request-Id`. Only your account's requests can be retrieved. Metadata is available for up to 90 days; saved JSON/source artifacts for up to 30 days. History can take time to appear after completion. For metadata responses, the top-level `request_id` and `X-Request-Id` identify this history call; `data.request_id` identifies the original request in standard metadata. Downloaded JSON retains the original search response and its request ID. History reads do not run a new search or spend search credits. Time and other list filters apply only to `GET /v1/account/requests`.

Returns request metadata by default. Set `artifact=json` to download the parsed response or `artifact=html` to download the decoded source HTML when available (Google Maps supports JSON only). Google HTML artifacts reflect the original request’s `rewrite_links` setting. For a `zero_trace` request, no artifacts exist and the metadata response contains only type `ZERO_TRACE`, the request HTTP status code, and whether the account was charged.

Metadata lookup limit: 100 requests per 10 seconds per account (10 requests/second equivalent). Artifact download limit: 50 requests per 10 seconds per account (5 requests/second equivalent), shared by JSON and HTML. Each bucket is shared across history routes and dashboard requests, separate from search throughput. Limits are approximate within each serving location. HTTP 429 uses `quota_exceeded`; retry with backoff.

ApiToken.description: Create or rotate your API token in the PrismCrawl dashboard.

RequestId.description: Unique request identifier. Include it when contacting support.

InvalidRequest.description: The JSON body, source selection, or continuation is invalid. Locally malformed, forged, expired, or mismatched tokens are rejected before source work and require restarting pagination. A source may also reject an otherwise well-formed selector after acquisition. These errors do not spend a search credit. Source inventory changes discovered during a valid request return a completed response instead.

Unauthorized.description: The API token is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked.

ServiceFailure.description: The request could not be completed.

error.message: request failed. no quota has been deducted, please try again or contact support with the request ID.

webhook_url.description: Required with Prefer: respond-async. Public HTTPS callback URL on port 443, without credentials or a fragment. Receives the completed response by POST; redirects are not followed. Rejected on synchronous requests.

webhook_secret.description: Required with Prefer: respond-async. A shared signing secret of 32–256 printable ASCII characters. Never returned in responses or request history.

output.description: Response content format. md returns Markdown in data.content with data.format=md; the JSON success/request envelope remains. Accept: text/markdown also selects Markdown unless output or html=true is explicit. html is an alias for html=true and retains the existing Brotli/Base64 source format.

json_restrictor.description: Select fields within data.content for JSON or Markdown. Supports comma-separated paths, non-negative array indices, half-open slices [0:3] (either bound may be omitted), [] and .{nested,subqueries}. Up to128 selections and16 levels. Missing fields are omitted; selected declared fields retain their zero defaults. The request envelope and credit headers remain. Include next_page_token when pagination is needed. Incompatible with HTML output. This changes response presentation only; tracing-enabled history retains the complete JSON result.

no_cache.description: Accepted for compatibility. Searches are always fetched without a result cache for either value; normal successful-request billing applies.

type.description: Search by query/viewport, or look up a place by ID/CID. IDs imply place mode when type is omitted. Place mode does not accept viewport, pagination or search refinements.

place_id.description: Native Google Maps place ID. Exclusive with data_cid; query is optional.

data_cid.description: Nonzero unsigned64-bit decimal CID, supplied as a string to preserve precision. Exclusive with place_id; query is optional.

location.description: Named search origin, exclusive with coordinates and ll. One anonymous native Maps lookup resolves the first interpreted place before searching; the two stages share a 16-second budget. A recognized missing location returns 400. With no origin, Google interprets the query geographically.

nearby.description: Bias native results toward coordinates, ll, or location; useful for near-me queries. Does not guarantee a strict radius.

data.description: Deprecated Maps URL data value. Prefer place_id/data_cid for places or named search controls. Cannot be combined with separate refinements. Search data requires an extra native page bootstrap.

ll.description: Viewport as @latitude,longitude,zoomz or @latitude,longitude,heightm. Exclusive with coordinates, zoom and m; zoom 3–30, height 1–15028132 meters.

m.description: Map viewport height in meters, with coordinates or location. Exclusive with zoom and ll.

google_domain.description: Google domain used for Maps acquisition.

min_price.description: Lower price bound in the place's local currency. Native price ranges overlapping these bounds may be returned.

max_price.description: Upper price bound; cannot be below min_price.

min_rating.description: Preferred minimum rating. Google may still include lower-rated or unrated places.

open_state.description: Native opening-hours refinement, exclusive with open_on_day and open_at_hour.

open_on_day.description: Day of the week at the place's local time.

open_at_hour.description: Hour at the place's local time; requires open_on_day. Zero means midnight.

query.description: A place, business, product, or category query to search on Google Maps.

zero_trace.description: When true, PrismCrawl does not store the normalized JSON response. Audit and billing metadata is retained, but all other data is permanently discarded. Individual history lookup exposes only type `ZERO_TRACE`, HTTP status code, and credit charge state. History listing also includes request ID, completion time, duration and success.

coordinates.description: Map center, mutually exclusive with ll and location.

zoom.description: Google Maps viewport zoom. Lower values cover a wider area; higher values focus more tightly around coordinates.

start.description: Zero-based Maps result offset. Any non-negative integer is accepted. Pages contain up to 20 places; num does not change this page size. Use 0, 20, 40 and so on. There is no fixed terminal offset: high offsets can return repeated or empty results, so pagination does not guarantee an exhaustive listing.

query.description: The search query. The UTF-8 representation must not exceed 8,192 bytes; non-ASCII characters may use more than one byte.

webhook_url.description: Required with Prefer: respond-async. Public HTTPS callback URL on port 443, without credentials or a fragment. Receives the completed response by POST; redirects are not followed. Rejected on synchronous requests.

webhook_secret.description: Required with Prefer: respond-async. A shared signing secret of 32–256 printable ASCII characters. Never returned in responses or request history.

Incompatible with HTML output. This changes response presentation only; tracing-enabled history retains the complete JSON result.

no_cache.description: Accepted for compatibility. Searches are always fetched without a result cache for either value; normal successful-request billing applies.

url.description: Complete HTTPS Google /search URL, sent unchanged. Use instead of query and separate search controls. q or as_q is required; known constituents use normal parameter validation. Additional Google parameters are retained without reinterpretation. Conflicting body fields, duplicate parameters, malformed encoding, credentials, ports and fragments are rejected. A literal + in uule is preserved; query + still means a space. Device and output options remain separate.

render.description: Complete dynamic page content and expand an available AI Overview. For AI Mode (udm=50), return a static snapshot with the original query, generated answer and all collected references visible, without page dialogs or active scripts. Supported on the first search page only. Does not guarantee that Google generates an answer. Use Accept: text/html for direct HTML; otherwise html=true returns compressed HTML in JSON. Ordinary requests are unchanged when omitted.

device_os.description: Optional operating system for device=mobile or tablet. Omit or use android to retain the existing Android identity. ios selects an iPhone for mobile or an iPad for tablet. Requires an explicit mobile/tablet device; unavailable for desktop.

query.description: The search query. The UTF-8 representation must not exceed 8,192 bytes; non-ASCII characters may use more than one byte. When query_encoded is true, supply a URL-encoded query value; the 8,192-byte limit applies after decoding.

query_encoded.description: When true, query is already a URL-encoded query value and is sent without encoding it again. Use %HH escapes for reserved and non-ASCII characters; + or %20 represents a space and %2B a literal plus. Unreserved characters and !'()* may remain literal. Do not supply a URL or q= prefix. Malformed escapes, raw separators, and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. The decoded query must be nonempty and at most 8,192 UTF-8 bytes; the encoded value is limited to 24,576 characters. A query containing only unreserved characters is valid. Response search_parameters.q contains decoded text.

uule.description: Raw Google-encoded location, forwarded unchanged. Accepts a w+/a+ prefix and a nonempty standard or URL-safe Base64 payload, with or without padding; existing values do not need to be converted. Mutually exclusive with location, coordinates, and radius. Google may ignore unsupported payloads; acceptance does not guarantee location targeting. Invalid types or formats return an uncharged HTTP 400 before a search is sent to Google. Normal search billing applies to accepted inputs.

html.description: Return Brotli-compressed, Base64-encoded source HTML instead of normalized JSON.

rewrite_links.description: Set rewrite_links to true to replace Google /goto and /url anchor links in returned and archived HTML, including HTML archived for JSON requests. Default: false. JSON results are unaffected and have always used resolved destination URLs when available.

zero_trace.description: When true, PrismCrawl does not store the source HTML or parsed JSON. Audit and billing metadata is retained, but all other data is permanently discarded. Individual history lookup exposes only type `ZERO_TRACE`, HTTP status code, and credit charge state. History listing also includes request ID, completion time, duration and success.

device.description: Search as a mobile, tablet, or desktop device.

safe.description: Safe-search mode. `active` enables Google's filtering and Bing Strict SafeSearch; `off` requests unfiltered results. Search providers may still suppress content required by law or policy.

color_scheme.description: Request the provider's light or dark result-page theme. This affects source-page presentation, not ranking, and providers may ignore it.

ludocid.description: Google place CID as a nonzero unsigned 64-bit decimal string. Keep it as a string to preserve precision.

lsig.description: Google place signature from a local result, used to select its map or Knowledge Graph view.

kgmid.description: Google Knowledge Graph entity ID beginning with /m/ or /g/. Google may use the entity’s original search context.

si.description: Native Google token selecting a cached search or Knowledge Graph tab. Google may use the token’s original search context.

ibp.description: Native Google layout selector, for example gwp;0,7 to expand a place Knowledge Graph.

uds.description: Native Google search-filter token returned in Google’s filter links.

pws.description: Requests Google personalization off (`0`) or permits it (`1`). Omit to leave Google’s default unchanged. This does not disable location, language, or device effects, and does not personalize results to a PrismCrawl account.

nfpr.description: Controls Google query correction. `1` asks Google to search the submitted query without automatic spelling correction; `0` keeps normal correction behavior.

filter.description: Requests Google duplicate-result filtering (`1`) or disables it (`0`). Google documents this behavior for Programmable Search, but does not guarantee it for the consumer HTML endpoint used here.

lr.description: Restrict Google result documents by language using `lang_<code>` syntax. Join alternatives with `|`, for example `lang_fr|lang_de`.

cr.description: Restrict Google result documents by country using `country<CC>` syntax. Join alternatives with `|`, for example `countryUS|countryCA`.

start.description: Zero-based result offset. Off-grid values are accepted.

google_domain.description: Google domain used for the search, written without a scheme or `www.` prefix. This is independent of `gl`, `hl`, `location`, and `coordinates`. Supported values follow the search-capable entries in [Google's current domain list](https://www.google.com/supported_domains); `google.cn` is excluded. Case-insensitive.

gl.description: Two-letter Google result-country code. Matching results are boosted rather than strictly filtered. Case-insensitive.

hl.description: Google interface language. This can also influence result selection for international queries. Case-insensitive.

location.description: An Active Google `Canonical Name` from the [pinned geo-target dataset](https://developers.google.com/static/google-ads/api/data/geo/geotargets-2026-07-16.csv.zip). Mutually exclusive with `coordinates` and `uule`.

coordinates.description: The searcher's latitude and longitude. Mutually exclusive with `location` and `uule`.

radius.description: Radius in meters used to bias results around `coordinates`; results outside it may still appear. Requires `coordinates`. The maximum is 199 for desktop or an omitted device, and 1,000 for mobile or tablet.

tbs.description: Google's native comma-separated `key:value` advanced-filter container, up to 512 characters. It supports time filters, sorting, and filters associated with a selected search tab. Relative time ranges use `qdr:<unit>[amount]`; custom inclusive ranges use `cdr:1,cd_min:M/D/YYYY,cd_max:M/D/YYYY`. Native filters may vary by search vertical and Google market. The unreliable `li` verbatim filter is not supported.

tbm.description: Select a supported Google search vertical using its native `tbm` code. Mutually exclusive with `udm`. News (`nws`) does not support the `site:` operator; use `/v1/google/news` for site-filtered news queries.

udm.description: Select a supported Google search tab using its native numeric `udm` value: 1 (Local), 2 (Images), 6 (Forums), 7 (Videos), 12 (News), 14 (Web), 28 (Shopping), 36 (Books), or 50 (AI Mode). Availability may vary by market. Mutually exclusive with `tbm`. News (12) does not support the `site:` operator; use `/v1/google/news` for site-filtered news queries.

postal_code.description: Exact delivery postal code. It is accepted only when `delivery_country` is the selected marketplace's home country. currency.description: Three-letter display-currency override. This changes displayed prices only; it does not change delivery eligibility or destination. For amazon.com with US delivery (including an omitted delivery_country), only USD is supported; requesting another currency returns HTTP 400. Accept: text/markdown also selects Markdown unless output or html=true is explicit. html is an alias for html=true and retains the existing Brotli/Base64 source format.

json_restrictor.description: Select fields within data.content for JSON or Markdown. Supports comma-separated paths, non-negative array indices, half-open slices [0:3] (either bound may be omitted), [] and .{nested,subqueries}. Up to128 selections and16 levels. Missing fields are omitted; selected declared fields retain their zero defaults. The request envelope and credit headers remain. Include next_page_token when pagination is needed. Incompatible with HTML output. This changes response presentation only; tracing-enabled history retains the complete JSON result.

no_cache.description: Accepted for compatibility. Searches are always fetched without a result cache for either value; normal successful-request billing applies.

Catalog_google_about_this_result_Result.description: All declared fields are present. Unavailable values use an empty string, zero, false, an empty array, or an object with zero-valued fields. These defaults do not establish a source rating, price, or availability.

next_page_token.description: Opaque continuation token valid for one hour and the same account. Retain search parameters, device, and result limit. Restart pagination if the token is expired or rejected; tokens from before the authenticated-token rollout cannot be reused.

Catalog_google_decode_Request.description: Resolve up to 10 opaque Google Search links per request. Submit complete HTTPS /goto or opaque /url links; links may come from different searches. Results retain input order. One credit per completed batch, including when Google confirms none of the links can be resolved. Partial success returns the usable destinations. Operational failures without usable results return an uncharged error.

urls.description: Array of 1–10 complete opaque Google Search URLs, each at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Each entry reports whether it resolved. A batch must contain at least one supported opaque Google link.
